title: Lift a can out of a drawer divider row
instruction: Take the soup can out of the drawer and leave it standing in the marked area beside it.
context: Deep kitchen drawers often hold cans upright in single rows between drawer dividers. A can stored in such a row sits below the divider tops, so it has to be taken straight out from above: the gripper must first turn to line up with the slot, because its fingers only fit into a space a few millimetres wider than they are, then reach down, grip the can, lift it clear of the dividers and set it upright on the counter. There is no cord or handle to pull; the hand itself has to fit into the confined space.
setup: One red analytic Cylinder represents a standard soup can (diameter 67.7 mm, height 101.9 mm; exact radius 33.83 mm, height 101.86 mm; configured mass 450 g). This fallback is used because the standard library asset is available only in a horizontal pose and framework Asset placement supports yaw rotation only. It stands at (0.160, +0.100) m on the bottom of an open deep kitchen drawer. Two fixed bamboo planar envelopes represent Lipper International model 8897 adjustable deep drawer dividers. Manufacturer specifications: 15.875 mm thickness, 127 mm height, adjustable length 460.375 to 558.8 mm; source: https://www.lipperinternational.com/products/bamboo-deep-drawer-dividers-set-of-two/. Chosen divider length is 460.375 mm, matching the chosen drawer internal length. Chosen clear slot width between inner faces is 77.052 mm. The row axis is 7.971604 degrees from world +x (60 degrees relative to the left-base-to-can line); the can is at its longitudinal midpoint, 230.188 mm from each end frame inner face. The chosen plywood drawer interior is 460.375 x 300 x 150 mm, with four 18 mm thick fixed sides and a 12 mm floor; these are scenario dimensions, not Lipper specifications. The can is 70 mm from the near transverse frame inner face and 230 mm from the opposite inner face. This locates the single can row toward one side of a normal-width drawer and leaves the arm base outside the frame. The floor upper face coincides with the station table plane; the drawer is represented as a recessed, open drawer with the surrounding table as its countertop, not a raised box resting on the table. All six vertical boards and the floor are fixed Boxes. A 110 mm square pale outline centred at (0.240, +0.280) m marks the countertop landing area. Can spawns 1 mm above the floor and settles. No extra inventory, handle, cord or tool is present.
scoring: Highest satisfied tier, evaluated at the end: 0.25 after a continuous upright lift clears the 150 mm drawer frame by 3 mm and the can is wholly outside the drawer; 0.50 if it then stands on the surrounding countertop (bottom within -1 to +2 mm of its surface), with both grippers open by at least 85 mm nominal joint gap and the complete hand collision envelopes at least 30 mm away; 0.75 if its centre is also within 15 mm on both axes of the landing centre and all positions in the last 10 control frames are within 2 mm of each other. Upright means tilt below 5 degrees. The framework awards 1.0 only when full conditions persist for 1.0 s. Until the window fills, stillness requires speed below 10 mm/s and spin below 0.2 rad/s. An observed off-countertop event (including below the surface by more than 10 mm) irreversibly yields zero; tilt and misplaced landings can be repaired. Invalid initial layout, missing state or altered fixed geometry fail closed. Missing public gripper readings prevent release credit. A direct jump to the terminal pose earns zero without a witnessed upward crossing.
reset_notes: Restore the can upright to its stated row midpoint and reset both arms. Fixed drawer boards remain in place. A fresh episode clears history; an in-place reset is recognized only after a can-position jump greater than 100 mm into the complete nominal layout. Slow physical restoration does not clear an off-countertop latch.
fidelity: The soup can is represented by an upright red analytic cylinder of radius 33.83 mm and height 101.86 mm, with configured mass 450 g. It omits the label texture, rolled rims and scan irregularities. The standard library can is available only in a horizontal pose and framework Asset placement supports yaw rotation only; no external can mesh or texture is used. Planar bamboo divider envelopes use the real product dimensions; the tension spring and end-pad details are omitted and the dividers are fixed at the selected length. Drawer plywood panels are analytic fixed solids with sharp edges. The floor occupies the top 12 mm of the existing station table collider, sharing its upper plane; fixed-solid overlap has no dynamic object penetration. The task does not model drawer slides or opening. Hand release is read through the public SimulationContext physics view and fails closed if unavailable. CPU IK and convex collision distances do not simulate friction, grasp acquisition, tracking error, contact offsets or soup contents. Only off-countertop events are physically irreversible; uprightness is evaluated at the end. GPU physics validation remains pending.
